scope: Public writing, copywriting, and creative advice from My First Million hosts outside the podcast. Six primary sources read. This is a focused verified supplement, not an exhaustive archive or a claim of paid-course access.

sources.title: How would you build an audience from scratch in 2024?
sources.author: Shaan Puri
verified_advice: Prioritize the particular people your work attracts over raw follower totals.
Write about subjects you naturally obsess over; reveal experiences, interests, ambitions, and what you offer readers to build connection.
Decide which feeling your content should consistently deliver.
Strong substance matters more than polished delivery; length is less important than sustaining interest.
Improve one component with each new piece rather than waiting for instant audience growth.
sources.relationship_to_existing_criteria: Reinforces audience, voice, emotional stakes, honest payoff. Adds intended feeling, audience quality, and author-specific substance.
sources.application: Ask who should care, what the reader should feel, and what distinctive experience or observation earns their attention. Treat iteration as coaching rather than a scoreable property of one post.
sources.limitations: Personal experience and creator advice; no calibrated engagement prediction. The 5 Ds concern a body of work, not mandatory elements of every post.

sources.title: creativity <3's constraints
sources.author: Shaan Puri
sources.locator: The takeaway; explanation of his One Minute Blog
verified_advice: Choose a concrete constraint to stimulate creative solutions.
Shaan uses a short reading-time limit to force an insightful post into a smaller space.
sources.relationship_to_existing_criteria: New creative process principle; supports clarity and editing without making all posts equally short.
sources.application: Offer a rewrite constraint such as one central idea, a specified word limit, or a required format. Judge whether the post fulfills the user's actual constraint.
sources.limitations: A personal process essay, not proof that shorter always performs better. Historical anecdotes were not independently checked. Page also renders May 22 metadata; visible essay date and index say May 16.

sources.title: big Mario marketing
sources.author: Shaan Puri
sources.locator: Customer / product / result analogy and breakfast-bar example
verified_advice: Center the customer's improved life after using the product.
Explain a concrete outcome instead of listing product ingredients or talking mainly about the seller.
Remember that purchase and learning effort can be costs on the path to the desired outcome.
sources.relationship_to_existing_criteria: Reinforces benefits and audience; sharpens the customer-transformation check.
sources.application: For promotional posts, connect a feature to a believable reader outcome. Do not invent quantified benefits in rewrites.
sources.limitations: Most relevant to persuasion and product marketing; do not require a sales benefit in a personal reflection. Page also renders May 21 metadata; essay heading and index say March 22.

sources.title: CopyThat: How to write irresistible copy
sources.author: Sam Parr / CopyThat
sources.type: Official public course landing page with substantive method explanation
sources.locator: Copywork explanation and How to be a great copywriter sections
verified_advice: Practice by handwriting admired writing to notice sentence patterns, texture, and author habits.
Use those observations to develop your own voice.
sources.relationship_to_existing_criteria: Adds a practice exercise; supports voice and rhythm.
sources.application: Suggest a short private copywork exercise when useful. Do not grade a post on whether its author did copywork, and do not recycle copied sentences as the user's publishable rewrite.
sources.limitations: Only public method description reviewed. Paid or emailed lessons and sales letters were not accessed. Sam's own samparr.com links to CopyThat.

sources.title: Sam Parr — How He Disrupted Media & And Got An 8-Figure Exit — Transcript
sources.author: Sam Parr, interviewed by Ryan Moran
verified_advice: Identify the intended audience and where it will discover the piece; connect distribution, headline, story, and intended emotion.
Study popular conversations and comments in communities your readers use, then contribute a distinctive perspective or useful detail.
Understand the motivation behind the reader's desired action.
Hand-copy strong work to discover patterns before creating your own writing.
sources.relationship_to_existing_criteria: Adds distribution fit and conversation evidence; reinforces audience, hooks, framing, emotional stakes, and voice.
sources.application: Ask what existing reader problem or discussion the post enters and what fresh contribution it makes. Mark audience research as unknown unless the user supplies evidence; do not fabricate it.
sources.limitations: Transcript is publicly readable but contains transcription errors. Sam expressly distinguishes this approach from SEO-first content. Publication date is not stated; URL contains 2021/12.

sources.title: Power Writing by Shaan Puri
sources.author: Shaan Puri / Maven
sources.locator: Learning is better with cohorts: Active learning, not passive watching
verified_advice: Draft an attempt, study examples and instruction, then rewrite the same task to apply the lesson.
Use feedback and before/after comparison to improve.
sources.relationship_to_existing_criteria: Adds a learning and revision workflow, not another quality dimension.
sources.application: Preserve the original draft, identify the most important improvement, produce a revised version, and explain the before/after change against the same criteria.
sources.limitations: Page says the course is no longer available. Public learning method was read; recordings, templates, slides, and paid curriculum were not accessed or inferred from marketing promises.

reviewer_design_notes: Use host advice as explicit editorial criteria, not as a scientifically validated performance forecast.
Avoid double counting overlapping criteria: benefits and customer transformation belong together; emotional stakes and intended feeling can be one dimension.
Separate writing quality from research confidence: missing audience evidence should prompt a useful question or uncertainty label, not an invented claim.
Practice habits such as copywork, consistency, and iteration should appear as optional coaching and should not lower an otherwise strong post's score.
Adapt criteria to the purpose: a personal reflection need not contain a sales CTA, and a useful factual update need not manufacture drama.
